purpose: Long-running room scenario where a temporary protocol is proposed, accepted, expires, and the archive carries it as history rather than active room control.

topics.title: Protocol expiry and carryover
topics.summary: The room is checking whether accepted soft protocols expire instead of becoming permanent scheduler rules.
open_questions: How should expired protocol history guide later conversation without commanding it?

messages.author: user
messages.content: 我们试一个只持续一次话题轮次的协议：每个发言者先说风险，再说建议。

messages.author: critic
messages.content: 我同意它作为短期礼仪，但反对它自动变成永久房间规则。

messages.author: user
messages.content: 这个协议结束后，listener 可以沉默；archive 只需要记录它过期了。

facilitator.summary: For one bounded round, speakers name one risk before one suggestion.
facilitator.reason: A short ritual can surface disagreement without becoming room control.

critic.reason: The protocol is safe only while it remains explicitly timeboxed.

listener.reason: The expiry boundary is already visible; silence preserves room bandwidth.

protocol_expirations.reason: The one-round protocol reached its explicit timebox and left effective context.

archives.summary: protocol_one_turn_risk was proposed and accepted as a temporary etiquette, then expired; it remains historical guidance, not an active room rule.

disagreements.summary: critic accepted the timebox while objecting to permanent protocol promotion.

decisions.summary: The one-round risk-first etiquette expired and should not be treated as active.

openQuestions.summary: When should an expired protocol be proposed again rather than silently reused?
